pr_summary: Add lemmas and instances about nonnegativity of ArchimedeanClass.mk for integer/natural/rational casts, simple constructor simp-lemmas for FiniteElement, rational embedding facts for the finite residue field, and many standard-part lemmas (zero characterization, monotonicity, additive/ multiplicative behavior, and cast simp lemmas).

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.mk_intCast_nonneg
declarations.nl_statement: For any integer n, the archimedean class mk (n : S) is nonnegative: 0 ≤ mk (n : S).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Split on whether n = 0. If n = 0 the statement is trivial by simp. If n ≠ 0, mk_intCast gives mk (n : S) = 0, so the inequality holds. The Lean proof does exactly this case split and uses mk_intCast in the nonzero case.
declarations.divergence: None — the proof is a straightforward case split mirroring the math.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.mk_natCast_nonneg
declarations.nl_statement: For any natural n, the archimedean class mk (n : S) is nonnegative: 0 ≤ mk (n : S).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This follows from the integer case by mod_cast: cast the natural to an integer and apply mk_intCast_nonneg. The Lean proof uses mod_cast to reduce to the previous lemma.
declarations.divergence: None — direct application of the integer case via the standard cast lemma.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.mk_ratCast_nonneg
declarations.nl_statement: For any rational q, the archimedean class mk (q : R) is nonnegative: 0 ≤ mk (q : R).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Case-split on q = 0. If q = 0 it's trivial. If q ≠ 0 then mk_ratCast shows mk (q : R) = 0, so the inequality holds. The Lean proof does exactly this.
declarations.divergence: None — straightforward.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.FiniteElement.mk_add
declarations.nl_statement: Given x,y in K with 0 ≤ mk x and 0 ≤ mk y, the element-level addition of their FiniteElement constructors satisfies .mk x + .mk y = FiniteElement.mk (x + y) (suitable nonnegativity proof).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is a definitional statement about the Subtype/valuation-subring constructor and the induced ring addition; it holds by definition (rfl). The proof in Lean is the trivial rfl.
declarations.divergence: None — purely definitional.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.FiniteElement.mk_mul
declarations.nl_statement: Given x,y in K with 0 ≤ mk x and 0 ≤ mk y, .mk x * .mk y = FiniteElement.mk (x * y) and the required nonnegativity follows from add_nonneg.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Again a definitional statement about multiplication on the subtype; the Lean proof is rfl. The nonnegativity is provided by add_nonneg in the statement of the constructed element.
declarations.divergence: None.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.FiniteElement.mk_le_mk_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For FiniteElement constructors, FiniteElement.mk x hx ≤ .mk y hy ↔ x ≤ y (when the hypotheses hx,hy assert 0 ≤ mk x, 0 ≤ mk y).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is the compatibility of the induced order on the subtype with the ambient order; in the file it is a direct rfl. Lean uses the quotient/subtype definitions so the lemma is definitional.
declarations.divergence: None.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.FiniteResidueField.mk_ratCast
declarations.nl_statement: For any rational q, the residue-field constructor satisfies mk (q : FiniteElement K) = q (i.e., rationals embed into the residue field as expected).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Decompose q = n/d. Multiply both sides by d (using injectivity mod_cast) and reduce to the nat case. Use the previously proved FiniteElement.mk_natCast_nonneg and the multiplicative compatibility (mk.map_mul) to cancel and simplify. The Lean proof follows this plan: it handles numerator/denominator, uses mul_left_inj on d, map_natCast, map_mul, the FiniteElement nat cast lemma, and simplifies.
declarations.divergence: None significant — standard calculation using denom/numer decomposition and the earlier nat-cast facts.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.stdPart_eq_zero_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For x : K, stdPart x = 0 iff mk x ≠ 0 (i.e., x has nonzero archimedean class exactly when its standard part is zero).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: The forward direction is stdPart_of_mk_ne_zero. For the reverse, contrapose: if mk x = 0 fails (so 0 ≤ mk x), use stdPart_of_mk_nonneg with the default embedding of the residue field into R, then apply map_ne_zero and the characterization of mk being nonzero in the residue field. The Lean proof performs the contraposition and applies these lemmas directly.
declarations.divergence: None — direct logical manipulation of the two previously proved facts.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.stdPart_monotoneOn
declarations.nl_statement: stdPart is monotone on the set {x | 0 ≤ mk x}: if 0 ≤ mk x, 0 ≤ mk y and x ≤ y then stdPart x ≤ stdPart y.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unfold stdPart (cases on the dif), reduce to comparing images under the fixed OrderRingHom from the residue field to R, and apply OrderRingHom.monotone' together with the equivalence FiniteElement.mk_le_mk_iff to translate the hypothesis. The Lean proof unfolds the defs and calls the monotonicity of the composed ring hom.
declarations.divergence: None — straightforward translation of monotonicity along the quotient map and embedding.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.stdPart_add_of_mk_neg_left
declarations.nl_statement: If 0 < mk x then for any y, stdPart (x + y) = stdPart y (i.e., adding an element with strictly positive archimedean class doesn't change the standard part).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Consider whether mk y is nonnegative or positive. If mk y ≥ 0, apply stdPart_add (both nonnegative) and then stdPart_of_mk_ne_zero on x to see the x-contribution is zero in the residue and obtain zero_add. If mk y < 0 (i.e., mk y > 0 fails), both mk x and mk y are 'nonzero' in the residue-field sense; use identities about mk on sums (mk_add_eq_mk_right) and uniqueness to show the residue contribution collapses, finishing by appealing to mk ≠ 0. The Lean proof follows this case split, using mk_add_eq_mk_right and the existing stdPart lemmas; it is a bit case-heavy but mirrors the math exactly.
declarations.divergence: Minor: the proof uses the library's mk_add_eq_mk_right and some equality-of-mk reasoning that is slightly more bookkeeping than the compact high-level math statement, but logically equivalent.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.stdPart_ratCast
declarations.nl_statement: For any rational q, stdPart (q : K) = q (rationals are fixed by stdPart).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Use that mk (q : K) ≥ 0 (mk_ratCast_nonneg), apply stdPart_of_mk_nonneg with the default embedding into R, then use the fact that mk on the residue field returns q (FiniteResidueField.mk_ratCast) and that the OrderRingHom respects rational casts (map_ratCast). The Lean proof exactly follows these steps in sequence.
declarations.divergence: None.

declarations.name: ArchimedeanClass.stdPart_intCast
declarations.nl_statement: For any integer n, stdPart (n : K) = n.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is derived from the rational-case lemma by using mod_cast: the lemma stdPart_ratCast for rationals reduces to the integer case via the standard cast commuting lemma. The Lean proof uses mod_cast to obtain the int cast simp from the rational-simp.
declarations.divergence: None — standard reduction via cast lemmas.

pr_summary: Add lemmas asserting continuity at isolated points: ContinuousWithinAt.of_not_accPt and ContinuousAt.of_not_accPt.

declarations.name: ContinuousWithinAt.of_not_accPt
declarations.nl_statement: If x is not an accumulation point of s, then f is continuous within s at x.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Use the fact that removing x does not change continuity at x (continuousWithinAt_diff_self). Replace s by s \ {x}. Since x is not an accumulation point of s, x is not in the closure of s \ {x}, hence the neighbourhood filter 𝓝[s \ {x}] x is the bottom filter. Thus Tendsto f (𝓝[s \ {x}] x) (𝓝 (f x)) holds trivially, giving ContinuousWithinAt for s (via the equivalence). The Lean proof performs these rewrites and finishes by simplification using the definitions of ContinuousWithinAt and AccPt.

declarations.name: ContinuousAt.of_not_accPt
declarations.nl_statement: If x is not an accumulation point of the complement of {x} (i.e. x is isolated), then f is continuous at x.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Recall ContinuousAt f x is equivalent to ContinuousWithinAt f (complement {x}) x (continuousWithinAt_compl_self). Apply the previous lemma ContinuousWithinAt.of_not_accPt to the set {x}ᶜ, using the hypothesis that x is not an accumulation point of {x}ᶜ. The Lean proof simply rewrites the equivalence and applies the earlier lemma.

pr_summary: Add ⋆-algebra conjugation by linear isometries and show continuous ⋆-algebra equivalences of endomorphism algebras are isometrically inner; add helpers to build an isometry from a continuous linear equivalence whose adjoint is a scalar multiple, and provide an OrderIsoClass instance via these results.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint.LinearIsometryEquiv.conjStarAlgEquiv
declarations.nl_statement: Given an isometric linear equivalence e : H ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] K between Hilbert spaces, conjugation by e defines a ⋆-algebra equivalence conjStarAlgEquiv e : (H →L[𝕜] H) ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (K →L[𝕜] K).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Construct the star-algebra equivalence by reusing the existing conjugation algebra equivalence on continuous linear maps (conjContinuousAlgEquiv) and upgrading it to a ⋆-algebra equivalence using ofAlgEquiv. The only extra check is that the map respects the star operation; this is a simple identity using star_eq_adjoint and unfolding the conjugation definition, discharged by simp.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv.auxContinuousLinearEquiv
declarations.nl_statement: Given a continuous linear equivalence e : V ≃L[𝕜] W and scalars α ≠ 0 and α' with α' * α' = α⁻¹, together with the identities adjoint e.toContinuousLinearMap ∘ e = α • id_V and e ∘ adjoint e.toContinuousLinearMap = α • id_W, define auxContinuousLinearEquiv as the continuous linear equivalence whose forward map is α' • e and whose inverse is α' • e.adjoint.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Define the forward map to be α' • e.toContinuousLinearMap and the inverse to be α' • e.toContinuousLinearMap.adjoint. The left and right inverse properties are algebraic consequences of the given adjoint identities and the relation α' * α' = α⁻¹: compute the compositions, use smul_smul and the provided equalities and then simplify. Continuity of the maps follows from scalarscaling of continuous maps. The Lean proof follows this calculation directly using simpa/simp and the hypotheses.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv.auxIsometry
declarations.nl_statement: Under the same hypotheses as auxContinuousLinearEquiv, and assuming furthermore that α' is fixed by the star endomorphism (starRingEnd 𝕜 α' = α'), produce a linear isometry equivalence V ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] W whose underlying continuous linear map is α' • e.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Take the linear equivalence coming from auxContinuousLinearEquiv and check the isometry condition using the characterization norm_map_iff_adjoint_comp_self. Using the expression for the adjoint compositions (the he/he' hypotheses) and the algebraic relation α' * α' = α⁻¹, one reduces the required norm equality to the given identity. The proof is a straightforward chain of rewrites and simp, mirroring the intended math.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv.coe_symm_auxIsometry
declarations.nl_statement: The inverse continuous linear map of auxIsometry equals α'⁻¹ • e.symm.toContinuousLinearMap (when α' is self-conjugate).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Prove equality by extensionality on vectors and use injectivity of the constructed ContinuousLinearEquiv; then reduce by simp and use the smul identities and the invertibility of α' (coming from positivity / nonzero hypotheses) to conclude inv_mul_cancel. The Lean proof uses ext and basic algebraic simplification.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv.StarAlgEquiv.eq_linearIsometryEquivConjStarAlgEquiv
declarations.nl_statement: If f : (V →L[𝕜] V) ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (W →L[𝕜] W) is a ⋆-algebra equivalence (assumed continuous), then there exists a linear isometry U : V ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] W such that f = U.conjStarAlgEquiv (i.e. f is conjugation by an isometry).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Follow the classical argument: first reduce trivial/subsingleton cases. Use the continuous-algebra version to get a continuous linear equivalence y : V ≃L[𝕜] W with f = y.conjAlgEquiv. From the ⋆-structure (map_star), deduce that adjoint(y) ∘ y commutes with every endomorphism, hence lies in the center of End(V), so it is a scalar α • id. Show α is real (use self-adjointness) and nonzero (invertibility). Positivity of adjoint(y) ∘ y yields α > 0, so construct α' as the inverse square root of re α and check α' * α' = α⁻¹. Use the auxIsometry construction to form U := (1/√(re α)) • y, which is a linear isometry. Finally check that conjugation by U reproduces f — the scalar factors cancel out by the choice of α' and the algebraic relations. The Lean proof carries out these steps with the necessary typeclass/field juggling and uses previously defined auxiliaries; it is a direct formalization of the standard argument.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv.OrderIsoClass.instance
declarations.nl_statement: For any type F of algebra equivalences (with star and continuity), one gets an OrderIsoClass instance: such an equivalence preserves the order on self-adjoint elements iff it is given by conjugation by the associated linear isometry.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Given f in the equiv type, reduce to the concrete StarAlgEquiv via the class, apply the previous theorem to realize f as conjugation by some linear isometry U, then rewrite inequalities using that conjugation by a linear isometry preserves positivity and order. The Lean proof imports the constructed U from the main theorem and finishes by unfolding definitions and appealing to the positivity conjugation lemma.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Algebra.Equiv.ofAlgEquiv
declarations.nl_statement: If e : A ≃ₐ[R] B is an algebra equivalence between topological algebras and both e and e.symm are continuous, then we can package it as a ContinuousAlgEquiv A ≃A[R] B.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is a thin wrapper: extend the existing AlgEquiv to the ContinuousAlgEquiv structure by supplying the continuity proofs for the forward and inverse maps. The lemmas showing the coercion and projections are definitional (rfl).

pr_summary: Ensure the pretty-printer reads the binder-type printing option at the correct expression position for Finset.prod and Finset.sum, fixing missing binder annotations when using pp.analyze.

declarations.name: BigOperators.delabFinsetProd
declarations.nl_statement: Delaborator for Finset.prod: when printing an application of Finset.prod, produce the corresponding big-product notation (∏), including cases ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ x, ∏ x ∈ s with p, and ∏ x with p, and optionally include the binder type (x : T) when the pp.funBinderTypes option is enabled at the correct source position.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Implementation (meta/programmatic): the delaborator inspects the expression for Finset.prod, extracts the function argument f and ensures it is a lambda. It then queries the pretty-printer option pp.funBinderTypes at the options in the position of the function argument (using withAppArg and getOptionsAtCurrPos) to decide whether to print the binder's type. It next delaborates the binder identifier and the body, determines how the finset index was formed (via delabFinsetArg) to distinguish Finset.univ / Finset.filter / concrete finsets, and emits the corresponding big-operator concrete syntax. For the Univ/filterUniv cases, if pp.funBinderTypes is true it delaborates the type (withNaryArg 0 delab) and produces a binder of the form (x : ty); otherwise it omits the type. The key change is reading pp.funBinderTypes at the application-argument position (getOptionsAtCurrPos) via withAppArg so that printing options affected by pp.analyze are observed at the point where the binder would be printed, preventing the missing annotation bug.

declarations.name: BigOperators.delabFinsetSum

declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Implementation (meta/programmatic): analogous to delabFinsetProd. The delaborator extracts the function argument, confirms it's a lambda, and queries pp.funBinderTypes at the options at the function-argument position (withAppArg + getOptionsAtCurrPos) to decide whether the binder type should be printed. It delaborates the binder and body, classifies the finset argument using delabFinsetArg, and emits the appropriate big-sum notation. When the index is univ (or filterUniv) and pp.funBinderTypes is enabled it delaborates and inserts the binder type; otherwise it omits it. The change fixes the previous behavior where the option was read from the wrong location, causing missing binder annotations under pp.analyze.

pr_summary: Add a theorem that the Mahler measure of a cyclotomic polynomial equals 1, by reducing to the monic case and using that cyclotomic roots are roots of unity of absolute value 1.

declarations.name: Polynomial.cyclotomic_mahlerMeasure_eq_one
declarations.nl_statement: For any commutative ring R with an algebra structure to ℂ and any n ∈ ℕ, the Mahler measure of the cyclotomic polynomial Φ_n over R, after mapping coefficients to ℂ, equals 1: ((cyclotomic n R).map (algebraMap R ℂ)).mahlerMeasure = 1.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Handle n = 0 separately (simp). For n ≠ 0, use the formula mahlerMeasure = |leading_coeff| * ∏_{root ζ} max(1, |ζ|) (mahlerMeasure_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_roots) and the fact Φ_n is monic, so the leading coefficient is 1. The cyclotomic roots are primitive n-th roots of unity, hence lie on the unit circle, so each |ζ| = 1; therefore each max(1, |ζ|) = 1 and the product is 1. In the formal proof this uses cyclotomic.monic, CStarRing.norm_of_mem_unitary, Multiset.prod_eq_one, and IsPrimitiveRoot.norm'_eq_one applied to each primitive root; a NeZero (n : ℂ) witness is provided to satisfy hypotheses of the primitive-root lemmas.

pr_summary: Remove unnecessary [NeZero n] typeclass assumptions from lemmas about Fin n by using the fact that the presence of a Fin n element implies n ≠ 0; update several lemmas to obtain NeZero via the provided Fin argument.

declarations.name: Fin.neZero_of_exists
declarations.nl_statement: For any natural number n and any element i : Fin n, n is nonzero (NeZero n).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Assume for contradiction that n = 0. Rewriting this into the hypothesis turns i into an element of Fin 0, which is impossible. Conclude NeZero n by negating the equality 0 = n.
declarations.divergence: The Lean proof directly matches the mathematical argument: rewrite the NeZero predicate to a negation of equality, assume equality, use that Fin 0 has no elements (elim0). No substantial divergence.

declarations.name: Fin.castLT_sub_nezero
declarations.nl_statement: For n : ℕ and i j : Fin n with i < j, the cast (j - i).castLT (using the fact that n - i.1 ≠ 0) is nonzero.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Reduce the goal to showing the underlying natural value of the cast is nonzero. Use arithmetic simplification (lia) and simp/ simpa to discharge the resulting inequality showing the natural value is nonzero. In Lean this is done by refining to Ne.symm (ne_of_val_ne ?_) and simplifying with coe_sub_iff_le and lia.
declarations.divergence: Proof is a routine translation of the arithmetic argument; the use of Ne.symm/ne_of_val_ne and simpa is Lean-specific bookkeeping but follows the math closely.

declarations.name: Fin.one_le_of_ne_zero
declarations.nl_statement: If k : Fin n, then (assuming NeZero n obtained from k) k ≠ 0 implies 1 ≤ k.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Obtain NeZero n from k (since having k : Fin n forces n ≠ 0). Reduce to the case n = succ m using existence of a successor for nonzero n. In the base case and succ case handle by simple value comparisons: when n = 1 the inequality is trivial; when n = succ m rewrite to inequalities on values and use standard facts that val_ne_zero_iff and one_le_iff_ne_zero. The Lean proof does a case split on the witness from Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero and finishes by simp/rw and basic facts about val and Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.
declarations.divergence: The proof follows the elementary case-analysis in the mathematics; the extra haveI/`NeZero` plumbing is due to the change in hypotheses but does not alter the essential argument.

declarations.name: Fin.val_sub_one_of_ne_zero
declarations.nl_statement: For i : Fin n, assuming NeZero n obtained from i, if i ≠ 0 then (i - 1).val = i - 1.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Obtain NeZero n from i, and assume i ≠ 0. Use existence of succ form of n, then apply Fin.sub_val_of_le with the fact one_le_of_ne_zero (proved above) to rewrite (i - 1).val, and then use Nat.mod_eq_of_lt with an estimate coming from nontriviality (two_le) to show the mod is identity. The Lean proof carries out these rewrites and discharges the inequality with nat facts / lia.
declarations.divergence: Directly mirrors the mathematical reduction to the underlying nat arithmetic and the mod-evaluation; the only divergence is more explicit typeclass/`haveI` handling for NeZero.

declarations.name: Fin.cast_val_eq_self
declarations.nl_statement: For a : Fin n, converting its value back to Fin n yields the same element: (a.val : Fin n) = a (with the implicit NeZero n obtained from a).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Obtain NeZero n from a. Reduce the equality of Fin elements to equality of values in ℕ and apply the lemma val_cast_of_lt which says that for a < n, (a : Fin n).val = a. Then use Fin.ext to conclude the elements are equal. The Lean proof invokes have : NeZero n := a.neZero_of_exists and applies Fin.ext with val_cast_of_lt a.isLt.
declarations.divergence: Proof is a straightforward translation of the math: show equality by comparing underlying naturals and use mod-evaluation; minor bookkeeping to expose NeZero n from the Fin element.

declarations.name: Fin.castLE_natCast
declarations.nl_statement: Given m n : ℕ with NeZero m and m ≤ n, for any a : ℕ, after deriving NeZero n from m ≤ n, Fin.castLE h (a.cast : Fin m) = (a % m : ℕ).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Introduce NeZero n from the inequality m ≤ n, then prove the equality by extensionality on Fin, simplifying both sides to their val forms (val_castLE and val_natCast) and applying Nat.mod_eq_of_lt using the appropriate bound obtained from m ≤ n and modular arithmetic facts about a % m. The Lean proof does ext; simp to reduce to value equality and then uses Nat.mod_eq_of_lt with a variant of mod_lt bound.
declarations.divergence: Follows the natural proof about casting and modulus; the step of creating a local NeZero instance is an implementation detail and the rest is routine arithmetic simplification.

declarations.name: Fin.val_add_one_of_lt'
declarations.nl_statement: For n : ℕ and i : Fin n, if i + 1 < n then (i + 1).val = i.val + 1 (with NeZero n obtained from i).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Derive NeZero n from i. Then use the definition of addition on Fin and the fact that when the sum is strictly less than n, mod is identity: Nat.mod_eq_of_lt. The Lean proof calls simpa with add_def and Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (discharging the inequality with lia).
declarations.divergence: Direct arithmetic argument; the only notable aspect is explicit recovery of NeZero from the Fin element.

pr_summary: Small tidy-up across many files: reformatting, replace trivial rfl with simp, minor proof refactors (e.g. more explicit uses of mem_top, Quot.out), and small docstring/simp changes.

declarations.name: Submonoid.closure_irreducible
declarations.nl_statement: In a cancellative commutative monoid with only the trivial unit and which is finitely generated, the submonoid generated by the irreducible elements equals the whole monoid.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Pick a minimal generating set S for the monoid (exists by FG). Show S equals the set of irreducible elements by proving both inclusions. One direction is irreducible_subset_of_submonoidClosure_eq_top. For the other, assume r∈S is reducible and write r = a*b with a,b non-units; express a and b as products of elements of S (using membership in Submonoid.closure and the fact closure S = ⊤). Isolate the powers of r in these products and consider the sum m r + n r. Do case analysis: if sum = 0 then r lies in closure of S \ {r} contradicting minimality; if sum = 1 then one factor is unit contradicting non-unit assumption; if sum ≥ 2 then cancellation and the singleton-unit hypothesis force r = 1, contradiction. Thus all elements of S are irreducible and the closure of irreducibles is ⊤.

declarations.name: DirectSum.id
declarations.nl_statement: When the index type is unique (e.g., PUnit), the direct sum ⨁ i, M is additively isomorphic to M; the file provides the explicit equivalence and shows it is inverse to the canonical maps.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Define the equivalence using DirectSum.toAddMonoid and of; give toFun and invFun explicitly. For left_inv one uses induction on DirectSum via DirectSum.induction_on: check zero, singletons (using Unique.default_eq), and compatibility with addition. right_inv is handled by toAddMonoid_of. The port edits reorganize the induction branch to use AddMonoidHom.id_apply for clarity and tidy up the proof bodies.

declarations.name: Associated.associated_iff_eq
declarations.nl_statement: If a monoid has only the trivial unit (Units is subsingleton), then the associated relation (~ᵤ) is just equality: x ~ᵤ y ↔ x = y.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: The file replaces the explicit two-direction constructor-based proof with a one-line simp-based proof: simplify using the definition of Associated and units being equal to 1 (Units.eq_one), which collapses the existential defining associated to an equality. This reflects the standard math: when units are trivial, associated elements must be equal.

declarations.name: Polynomial.X_pow_smul_rTensor_monomial
declarations.nl_statement: For commutative semiring S and R-algebra structure, the action of X^k on the r-tensor of a monomial equals the r-tensor of the monomial of degree k: X^k • rTensor ((monomial 0).restrictScalars R) sn = (rTensor ((monomial k).restrictScalars R)) sn.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Prove by tensor-product induction on the simple tensor sn: handle zero, addition (by simp using inductive hypotheses), and pure tensors tmul s n. For tmul use properties of rTensor on tmul, rewrite the scalar action to multiplication, commute factors and apply the identity C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial. The change in the file is a refactor that un-indents and brings the induction clauses to top level, but the reasoning is standard and follows the usual TensorProduct.induction_on proof.

declarations.name: Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul'
declarations.nl_statement: If leadingCoeff p * leadingCoeff q ≠ 0, then leadingCoeff (p * q) = leadingCoeff p * leadingCoeff q.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Instead of unfolding leadingCoeff and doing manual rewrites, the proof now uses a simp-style step: simplify using coeff_natDegree and then apply natDegree_mul' and coeff_mul_degree_add_degree. This is the natural algebraic computation: the leading coefficient of the product equals product of leading coefficients when degrees add and leading coefficients are nonzero.

declarations.name: Scheme.exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq
declarations.nl_statement: Given a limit cone in a suitable diagram of schemes, one can find an affine open whose preimage under the limit map equals a given open, and the lemma assembles the required data (it’s a helper about preimages in affine transition limits).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: After obtaining the desired affine j and hj from Scheme.exists_isAffine_of_isLimit applied to the limit of opens, the proof reduces the remaining equation by rewriting via Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage and the cone equation c.w, and then uses simp (replacing rfl) to discharge the trivial equality. This is a minor tidy: the mathematical step is simply using functoriality and the cone equation to match preimages.

declarations.name: Scheme.exists_isOpenCover_and_isAffine
declarations.nl_statement: Construct an open cover and affine pieces for an object in a cofiltered limit of schemes with affine transition maps, such that certain pullbacks are affine; the lemma produces the finite subcover and compatibility data used in later constructions.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: The proof picks indices via the cofilteredness, manipulates preimages using functoriality of Hom.preimage and composition of the cone, and then simplifies the trivial equality occurrences with simp. The mathematics is unchanged; the proof tidies equality steps by replacing rfl with simp to use available lemmas about preimage composition.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.cofibrations_over_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For the over category Over S, a morphism f is a cofibration iff its underlying map f.left is a cofibration in the base category C.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is proved by unfolding definitions: rewrite cofibration_iff and the `over`-definition of cofibrations, then apply MorphismProperty.over_iff. The PR replaces a two-step simp+rfl with a single simp only using the explicit defs; the math is immediate from the definition of the over-construction.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.fibrations_over_iff
declarations.nl_statement: Analogous statement for fibrations: f is a fibration in Over S iff f.left is a fibration in C.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Same approach as for cofibrations: expand the definitions and simplify with simp only; the file replaces a trivial rfl with a direct simp that mentions fibrations_over_def and MorphismProperty.over_iff.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.weakEquivalences_over_iff
declarations.nl_statement: Analogous statement for weak equivalences: f is a weak equivalence in Over S iff f.left is a weak equivalence in C.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: As above: unfold weakEquivalence_iff together with the `over` definition and simplify; the changed proof consolidates the equalities with simp only.

declarations.name: AbsoluteValue.isEquiv_iff_lt_one_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For strict ordered rings S, two absolute values v and w are equivalent iff for all x we have v x < 1 ↔ w x < 1.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: One direction is trivial: equivalence implies the pointwise ↔. For the converse, case-split on whether v x = 0; if v x = 0 use simp, otherwise reduce the ≤/≥ statements by multiplying by inverses and using multiplicative properties of absolute values; then apply the hypothesis on the '<1' predicate. The edited proof reorganizes the rcases on v x = 0 and simplifies branches; the mathematical content is the standard equivalence-of-absolutes argument.

declarations.name: PiTensorProduct.nonempty_lifts
declarations.nl_statement: Every tensor x : ⨂[R] i, s i has at least one lift in the set of lists (FreeAddMonoid) representing it — i.e., lifts x is nonempty.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Use the quotient representation of the tensor product: provide Quot.out x as a witness (previously a longer construction using Quotient.out). Then simplify the membership condition using the characterization of lifts and the quotient relation (AddCon.quot_mk_eq_coe). The PR shortens the witness construction to Quot.out and uses simp to tidy the equation, following the usual approach of constructing a preimage under a quotient.

declarations.name: RealRMK.le_rieszMeasure_tsupport_subset
declarations.nl_statement: If f : C_c(X, ℝ) satisfies 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 pointwise and tsupport f ⊆ V, then Λ f ≤ rieszMeasure Λ V (compare Λ to the constructed measure).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: The proof reduces to comparing Λ f to the measure of V via the content measure: use regularity to replace measure by content on the compact support, then unfold the definitions of rieszContent and apply the auxiliary lemma that approximates the content from above. The PR replaces an intermediate let-binding and uses convert with the composite expression directly, and simplifies some map/comap steps with simp; the underlying argument matches the textbook inequality between the functional and the representing measure.

declarations.name: IsHausdorff.of_map
declarations.nl_statement: If M is a module over R and S is an R-algebra, and J is an ideal of S with I.map(algebraMap R S) ≤ J, then Hausdorffness relative to J implies Hausdorffness relative to I (transport of Hausdorff property along map of ideals).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Given x that is zero modulo all powers of I, use the inclusion I.map ≤ J and properties of ideal maps to show x is zero modulo powers of J, then apply Hausdorffness for J. The proof rearranges the uses of AddSubmonoid.smul_mem_smul, moving hypotheses into arguments and replacing some apply-trivial steps with exact and simp. The mathematics is the standard transfer of vanishing across the map of ideals.

declarations.name: IsIntegrallyClosedIn.instance_for_integralClosure
declarations.nl_statement: The integral closure integralClosure R A is integrally closed in A (i.e., it is integrally closed in A by construction).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Construct the IsIntegrallyClosedIn structure by using injectivity of algebraMap (here via FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective) and show that any element integral over integralClosure is already in integralClosure by transitivity of isIntegral. The changed proof replaces a use of Subtype.val_injective with the more general FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective to be robust; otherwise the logic is the usual verification that integralClosure is integrally closed.

declarations.name: Chebyshev.degree_T
declarations.nl_statement: For Chebyshev polynomial T R n (n : ℤ) over an integral domain where 2 ≠ 0, degree (T R n) = |n| (the usual degree of Chebyshev polynomials).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Prove by induction on n using the recurrence T_{n+2} = 2 X T_{n+1} - T_n. In the successor step show the leading term comes from 2 * X * T_{n+1} and compute its degree via degree_C_mul and degree_mul_X, rely on natDegree_mul' previously proven. The PR replaces ad-hoc 'change' steps with explicit rw using C_ofNat and degree_C_mul two_ne_zero, and replaces rfl with norm_cast in degree comparisons; the math follows the standard degree induction argument.

declarations.name: Chebyshev.leadingCoeff_T
declarations.nl_statement: For Chebyshev T polynomials, the leading coefficient of T R n equals the expected value coming from recurrence (compatible with raising to powers), and the lemma computes leadingCoeff (T R n) by induction on n.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Induct on n and use the recurrence. For the inductive step rewrite the degree of the main term and apply leadingCoeff_sub_of_degree_lt. The PR streamlines the degree comparisons and rewrites to use C_ofNat and two_ne_zero, and uses norm_cast to tidy numeric coercions. The mathematical structure of the proof is the usual inductive computation of leading coefficients for Chebyshev polynomials.

declarations.name: PolynomialLaw.exists_lift_of_mem_range_rTensor
declarations.nl_statement: If an element is in the range of an rTensor map from a subalgebra, then there exists a lift p in the appropriate polynomial algebra yielding it — used to lift elements from tensor factors to polynomial lifts.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Use the surjectivity of the rTensor map restricted to ranges and manipulate composition with Subalgebra.val and toLinearMap to produce the preimage p; the proof ends with a simp replacing an rfl to close an equality. The PR simplifies the final step by replacing an explicit rfl with simp making the last equality check use lemmas about rTensor and toLinearMap; the conceptual proof is standard surjectivity/lift construction for tensor products.

declarations.name: LocalAtTarget.isHomeomorph_iff_restrictPreimage
declarations.nl_statement: Given a continuous map f with an open cover U of the target, f is a homeomorphism iff each restriction (U i).1.restrictPreimage f is a homeomorphism.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unfold IsHomeomorph into IsEmbedding and surjectivity; show both properties are local on the target by reducing to the corresponding statements for the restricted maps and using the open-cover equality iSup_set_eq_univ. The PR replaces a final trivial rfl with adding Opens.carrier_eq_coe to the simp argument so that the proof relies on available lemmas about Opens; the math is the usual local-to-global check for homeomorphisms.

pr_summary: Add full subcategories of cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant objects (as ObjectProperty full subcategories) with simple constructors, projection lemmas and compatibility lemmas for weak equivalences and inclusion functors.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.cofibrantObjects
declarations.nl_statement: For a category C with cofibrations and an initial object, cofibrantObjects C is the object property on C given by IsCofibrant.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is a definition/abbreviation: cofibrantObjects is defined to be IsCofibrant, so there is no proof beyond the straightforward definition.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.CofibrantObject.mk_surjective
declarations.nl_statement: For X : CofibrantObject C, there exists Y : C and a proof IsCofibrant Y such that X = mk Y.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unpack the full-subcategory element X (which is a pair of an object and the property). Take Y := X.obj and the stored property X.property; equality is rfl. Implemented as the triple ⟨X.obj, X.property, rfl⟩.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.CofibrantObject.weakEquivalence_homMk_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For cofibrant X Y and f : X ⟶ Y, WeakEquivalence (homMk f) ↔ WeakEquivalence f.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Reduce the statement using the definition of weak equivalence for morphisms in the full subcategory: WeakEquivalence (ObjectProperty.homMk f) is equivalent to WeakEquivalence f. The proof does a simp using weakEquivalence_iff and finishes by rfl.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.fibrantObjects
declarations.nl_statement: For a category C with fibrations and a terminal object, fibrantObjects C is the object property X ↦ IsFibrant X.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: This is an abbreviation defining fibrantObjects as the predicate IsFibrant on objects; no proof required beyond the definition.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.FibrantObject.mk_surjective
declarations.nl_statement: For X : FibrantObject C, there exists Y : C and a proof IsFibrant Y such that X = mk Y.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unpack the full-subcategory element and return ⟨X.obj, X.property, rfl⟩. Straightforward projection from the bundled data.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.FibrantObject.weakEquivalence_homMk_iff
declarations.nl_statement: For fibrant X Y and f : X ⟶ Y, WeakEquivalence (homMk f) ↔ WeakEquivalence f.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Same pattern as for cofibrant objects: use the construction of morphisms in the full subcategory and reduce via weakEquivalence_iff; apply simp then rfl.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.bifibrantObjects
declarations.nl_statement: bifibrantObjects C is the object property of being both cofibrant and fibrant, i.e. the infimum cofibrantObjects C ⊓ fibrantObjects C.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Defined as the meet (inf) of the two ObjectProperty predicates; a direct definition with no additional proof obligations.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.bifibrantObjects_le_cofibrantObject
declarations.nl_statement: The property bifibrantObjects C implies cofibrantObjects C (the left projection of the conjunction).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Given a proof h : bifibrantObjects C X, which is a pair, return h.1. Implemented as a lambda fun _ h ↦ h.1.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.bifibrantObjects_le_fibrantObject
declarations.nl_statement: The property bifibrantObjects C implies fibrantObjects C (the right projection of the conjunction).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Analogous to the previous lemma: extract h.2 from the pair h. Implemented as fun _ h ↦ h.2.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.BifibrantObject.mk_surjective
declarations.nl_statement: For X : BifibrantObject C, there exists Y : C with IsCofibrant Y and IsFibrant Y such that X = mk Y.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unpack the bundled element of the full subcategory: use X.obj, and X.property.1 and X.property.2 to provide the two proofs; equality is rfl. Implemented as ⟨X.obj, X.property.1, X.property.2, rfl⟩.

declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.BifibrantObject.homMk_surjective
declarations.nl_statement: For cofibrant and fibrant X Y, any morphism f : mk X ⟶ mk Y in the full subcategory arises from a unique underlying morphism g : X ⟶ Y (and equalities of the bundled hom).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Morphisms in the full subcategory are built by ObjectProperty.homMk; the stored data contains the underlying hom in f.hom. The proof returns ⟨f.hom, rfl⟩, projecting the underlying morphism and using rfl to witness equality.

pr_summary: Add API lemmas for covering and packing numbers: empty/singleton/zero cases and positivity, relations to encard, monotonicity, and the key inequality packingNumber (2*ε) ≤ externalCoveringNumber ε; also add isSeparated_zero in MetricSeparated.

declarations.name: Metric.packingNumber_eq_zero
declarations.nl_statement: For ε ≥ 0 and A ⊆ X, packingNumber ε A = 0 ↔ A = ∅.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unfold packingNumber to an ENat iSup over subsets C ⊆ A that are ε-separated. Use the characterization ENat.iSup_eq_zero and encard_eq_zero to reduce to the claim that if A is nonempty then some iSup term is nonzero. Contraposition: assume A is nonempty and pick x ∈ A; the singleton {x} is a separated subset with encard 1, hence the iSup is ≥ 1, contradicting equality to 0. The proof in Lean follows this exactly, using simp and a by_contra, then applying the `h` hypothesis to the singleton {x}.
declarations.divergence: Direct and transparent: the proof is a literal formalization of the standard contrapositive argument using iSup/encard properties.

declarations.name: Metric.packingNumber_singleton
declarations.nl_statement: For any ε ≥ 0 and x : X, packingNumber ε ({x}) = 1.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Upper bound: packingNumber ≤ encard {x} = 1 (packingNumber_le_encard_self). Lower bound: take the subset C = {x} witnessing the iSup in the definition of packingNumber, giving a lower bound of 1. The Lean proof uses le_antisymm: the upper bound is given by packingNumber_le_encard_self and simp; the lower bound is constructed by repeated le_iSup_of_le calls to show the iSup is at least the encard of {x}.
declarations.divergence: Very close to the mathematical argument; the nested le_iSup_of_le calls are bureaucratic but follow straightforwardly from the iSup definition.

declarations.name: Metric.packingNumber_two_mul_le_externalCoveringNumber
declarations.nl_statement: For any ε ≥ 0 and set A, packingNumber (2 * ε) A ≤ externalCoveringNumber ε A.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Expand definitions to exhibit the relation between the supremum over separated subsets D ⊆ A and the infimum over covers C. Fix a covering C and a (2ε)-separated subset D ⊆ A. For each x ∈ D, choose a witness in C within ε (using the cover property) and define a map f : D → C sending x to that witness. Show f is injective: if f x = f y then edist x y ≤ edist x (f x) + edist (f x) y ≤ 2ε, contradicting the (2ε)-separation unless x = y. Therefore |D| ≤ |C|, so taking sup over D and inf over C yields the inequality. The Lean proof follows this plan verbatim: it constructs f with choice, proves edist bounds, and applies Cardinal.mk_le_of_injective to obtain the desired inequality after unfolding ENNReal/cardinal conversions.
declarations.divergence: The proof is an almost exact mechanization of the standard covering/packing argument; the only Lean-specific details are choice of representatives for the cover and using Cardinal.mk_le_of_injective to compare encard, which matches the mathematical steps.

declarations.name: Metric.externalCoveringNumber_zero
declarations.nl_statement: In an EMetricSpace E, for any A ⊆ E, externalCoveringNumber 0 A = A.encard.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Show externalCoveringNumber ≤ A.encard by observing A itself is a 0-cover, hence one of the iInf terms. For the reverse inequality, take any C that is a 0-cover of A; the `isCover_zero` lemma says such a C must contain A, so A.encard ≤ C.encard. Taking the infimum over C yields externalCoveringNumber ≥ A.encard. The Lean proof does exactly this: it uses IsCover.externalCoveringNumber_le_encard for the easy direction and then rewrites with isCover_zero and encard_le_encard for the other direction.
declarations.divergence: Straightforward; the proof mirrors the textbook argument with only trivial rewriting and iInf reasoning.

declarations.name: Metric.coveringNumber_zero
declarations.nl_statement: In an EMetricSpace E, for any A ⊆ E, coveringNumber 0 A = A.encard.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Reduce to externalCoveringNumber_zero: coveringNumber ≤ A.encard is immediate (taking the cover inside A). For the reverse inequality, note externalCoveringNumber 0 A = A.encard and externalCoveringNumber ≤ coveringNumber, so coveringNumber ≥ A.encard. The Lean proof uses le_antisymm with these two inequalities and rewrites via externalCoveringNumber_zero.
declarations.divergence: Direct reduction to the externalCoveringNumber case; no conceptual gap.

declarations.name: Metric.packingNumber_zero
declarations.nl_statement: In an EMetricSpace E, for any A ⊆ E, packingNumber 0 A = A.encard.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Upper bound: packingNumber ≤ A.encard (packingNumber_le_encard_self). Lower bound: the iSup ranges over subsets C ⊆ A, so taking C = A shows the supremum is at least A.encard. The Lean proof applies le_antisymm and uses le_iSup_of_le to obtain the lower bound; this matches the mathematical idea exactly.
declarations.divergence: Routine and faithful formalization of the obvious cardinality bounds.

declarations.name: Metric.IsSeparated.encard_le_packingNumber
declarations.nl_statement: If C ⊆ A and C is ε-separated, then C.encard ≤ packingNumber ε A.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Immediate from the definition of packingNumber as a supremum (iSup): packingNumber is the supremum of encard over separated subsets inside A, so any particular such C gives a lower bound. In Lean this is a one-line application of le_iSup₂_of_le and le_iSup_of_le.
declarations.divergence: Direct, trivial formalization of the definitional fact.

declarations.name: Metric.isSeparated_zero
declarations.nl_statement: In an EMetricSpace X, for any set s, IsSeparated 0 s holds.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: With ε = 0 the predicate IsSeparated (0 : ℝ≥0∞) is just the pairwise condition vacuously satisfied for equal points and amounting to 0 < edist x y for distinct x,y; this follows by simplification of the definition. The Lean proof is a simp proof that unfolds IsSeparated and Set.Pairwise.
declarations.divergence: Very small; the lemma is mostly a convenient simp lemma. The formal statement matches the mathematical reading, though one must be aware of the chosen conventions for Pairwise in the library.

pr_summary: Remove several backward.privateInPublic options and deprecated alias declarations; make a few auxiliary defs private (visibility cleanup).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mapToComposableArrows_id
declarations.nl_statement: For any short complex S₁, the map of the identity on S₁ to composable arrows is the identity on S₁.toComposableArrows.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: The goal is a componentwise equality of natural transformations built from the identity map. One proves it by discharging the obvious component equalities in the category theory setting; in the file this is done by the single call to the cat_disch tactic which closes the trivial equalities coming from identity maps and the definition of ShortComplex.mapToComposableArrows. The proof is essentially a one-line check that the components coincide.

declarations.name: SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.walk_toSimpleGraph (made private)
declarations.nl_statement: Given a simple graph G and a connected component C, and two vertices u, v in C, there is a walk in the induced subgraph C.toSimpleGraph from ⟨u,hu⟩ to ⟨v,hv⟩.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: First use the fact that u and v lie in the same connected component to obtain a walk p in the original graph G between u and v (this is `C.reachable_of_mem_supp` and one extracts a witness with `.some`). Then convert that G.walk into a walk in the induced subgraph by recursion on the walk: the empty walk gives Walk.nil, and a cons step uses that adjacency is preserved when restricting to the component (the membership-of-support lemmas), producing the adjacent pair in C.toSimpleGraph and then consing with the recursive call. The file implements this by a private auxiliary `walk_toSimpleGraph'` with an elementary inductive construction; `walk_toSimpleGraph` simply extracts the witness from `reachable_of_mem_supp` and applies the auxiliary. The carried Lean proof matches the math directly and is straightforward.

pr_summary: Add definitions of minimalCover and maximalSeparatedSet (canonical finite witnesses when covering/packing numbers are finite) and use the maximal separated set to prove inequalities linking covering and packing numbers, including coveringNumber ≤ packingNumber and several two-scale comparisons and a monotonicity lemma for coveringNumber with set inclusion.

declarations.name: Metric.exists_set_encard_eq_coveringNumber
declarations.nl_statement: If coveringNumber ε A is finite (≠ ⊤), then there exists a finite subset C ⊆ A which is an ε-cover of A and whose ENNReal cardinality equals coveringNumber ε A.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Unfold the definition of coveringNumber as an infimum over the ENNReal-encard of covers contained in A. From the hypothesis that this infimum is finite, extract a witness C' (a finite cover). Consider the subtype of sets s ⊆ A that are ε-covers of A; this subtype is nonempty. Apply ENat.exists_eq_iInf on the ENNReal-valued function sending a subtype element to its encard to get a subtype element C that attains the infimum. From the properties returned by ENat.exists_eq_iInf recover that C ⊆ A, is finite, is an ε-cover, and its encard equals the coveringNumber.
declarations.divergence: Direct formalization of the standard argument using existence of minima for an infimum in ENNReal when it is finite; uses ENat.exists_eq_iInf which matches the mathematical extraction of a minimizer.

declarations.name: Metric.minimalCover
declarations.nl_statement: noncomputable definition minimalCover ε A: a set which is a finite internal ε-cover of A with minimal ENNReal cardinality when coveringNumber ε A ≠ ⊤, otherwise ∅.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Defined by if-then-else: when coveringNumber is finite choose the set produced by exists_set_encard_eq_coveringNumber; otherwise return the empty set. This uses classical choice (noncomputable).
declarations.divergence: Straightforward packaging of the existential witness into a named definition using choice; matches mathematical practice.

declarations.name: Metric.minimalCover_subset
declarations.nl_statement: The minimalCover ε A is a subset of A.

pr_summary: Add Function.Injective.of_eq_imp_le (shows f.Injective if f x = f y implies x ≤ y) and simplify the proof of injective_of_lt_imp_ne (use `grind`).

declarations.name: injective_of_lt_imp_ne
declarations.nl_statement: Theorem: For a linear order α and any function f : α → β, if for all x < y we have f x ≠ f y, then f is injective.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: To prove injectivity, assume f x = f y. By trichotomy on x and y, three cases arise: x < y, x = y, or x > y. The first and third contradict the hypothesis that strictly smaller arguments have different images, so the only remaining possibility is x = y. Hence f is injective. The Lean proof uses the tactic `grind [Injective]` to discharge these case analyses automatically.

declarations.name: Function.Injective.of_eq_imp_le
declarations.nl_statement: Theorem: For a partial order α and any f : α → β, if whenever f x = f y we have x ≤ y, then f is injective.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Assume f x = f y. Applying the hypothesis to that equality gives x ≤ y; applying it to the symmetric equality gives y ≤ x. By antisymmetry of the partial order these two inequalities yield x = y, so f is injective. The Lean proof is a one-liner using antisymm: `fun _ _ hxy ↦ h hxy |>.antisymm <| h hxy.symm`.

pr_summary: Add lemmas showing that for a continuous map the sets of upper/lower bounds of the image of a dense subset coincide with those of the full range, and deduce equalities of sup/inf on the dense subset and the whole domain (with linear-order variants that remove boundedness hypotheses).

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_upperBounds
declarations.nl_statement: Let α be a preordered topological space with ClosedIicTopology, γ a topological space, S ⊆ γ dense, and f : γ → α continuous. Then the set of upper bounds of f '' S equals the set of upper bounds of range f.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Prove equality by two inclusions. One inclusion is trivial from f '' S ⊆ range f (upperBounds is antitone in its argument). For the other inclusion use continuity: hf.range_subset_closure_image_dense hS gives range f ⊆ closure (f '' S), so it suffices to show upperBounds (f '' S) ⊆ upperBounds (closure (f '' S)). If x is an upper bound of f '' S, then for any point y in closure (f '' S) we use the characterization mem_closure_iff_frequently: frequently points of any neighbourhood are in f '' S, and since every point of f '' S is ≤ x, the set Iic x is closed (isClosed_Iic) and contains this frequent set, hence contains y. Thus y ≤ x, showing x is an upper bound of the closure. Combining gives equality.

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_lowerBounds
declarations.nl_statement: Dual statement: with ClosedIciTopology, for continuous f and dense S, lowerBounds (f '' S) = lowerBounds (range f).
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Identical argument to the upper bounds case but dualized: use hf.range_subset_closure_image_dense and the closedness of Ici to upgrade an upper bound of the image to an upper bound of its closure, using mem_closure_iff_frequently and mem_of_closed.

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_sup
declarations.nl_statement: If α is a conditionally complete lattice with ClosedIicTopology, γ a topological space, S dense in γ, f : γ → α continuous, and range f is bounded above, then the supremum over γ equals the supremum over S: ⨆ i, f i = ⨆ s : S, f s.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Rewrite both sups as sSup of ranges. Handle the trivial empty-domain case separately. For nonempty domain, use the characterization of sSup as the unique least upper bound: isLUB_csSup produces IsLUB for the whole-range supremum. Use isLUB_congr together with Dense.continuous_upperBounds (proved above) to transport that IsLUB to the set f '' S, and then compare with isLUB_ciSup_set (the characterization of ciSup over a set) to deduce equality of the sSups by uniqueness of the LUB. A small monotonicity check of boundedness is handled by h.mono with a short grind step.

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_inf
declarations.nl_statement: Dual: If α is a conditionally complete lattice with ClosedIciTopology, f continuous and range f is bounded below, then infimum over γ equals infimum over S: ⨅ i, f i = ⨅ s : S, f s.
declarations.nl_proof_sketch: Same structure as the supremum case, dualized. Replace sSup/isLUB by sInf/isGLB and use Dense.continuous_lowerBounds. Use isGLB_csInf and isGLB_ciInf_set and uniqueness of GLB to conclude equality.

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_sup'
declarations.nl_statement: For α a conditionally complete linear order with ClosedIicTopology, γ a topological space, S dense in γ, and f : γ → α continuous, the supremum over γ equals the supremum over S: ⨆ i, f i = ⨆ s : S, f s. declarations.nl_proof_sketch: As before reduce to sSup of ranges and handle empty-domain. Proceed by cases on BddAbove (range f). If range f is bounded above, the argument is identical to Dense.continuous_sup. If not bounded above, show the image of S is also not bounded above: otherwise boundedness of the image would, via closure and continuity (image_closure_subset_closure_image and the density closure), imply boundedness of range f — contradiction. In the not-bdd-above case both csSup values are the `⊤`/csSup_of_not_bddAbove value, so they coincide. The proof uses range_comp' and simple simp/grind steps to manipulate ranges and closures.

declarations.name: Dense.continuous_inf'
declarations.nl_statement: Dual linear-order version: for a conditionally complete linear order with ClosedIciTopology, continuous f and dense S, the infimum over γ equals the infimum over S: ⨅ i, f i = ⨅ s : S, f s, with no BddBelow assumption.

If not, argue the image on S is not bounded below either by composing ranges and using closure/density, and conclude both csInf values are the same via csInf_of_not_bddBelow. The manipulations are straightforward and mirror the supremum linear-order case.
